title: Verna and the University
subtitle: A small republic, transformed by exile and protected by treaty
summary: The republic that existed before the scholars came, the exile that turned its colleges into a University, and the treaties that keep it valuable to everyone and owned by no one.
content:
> *"We do not need everyone to love us. We need everyone to prefer us unconquered."*
> — a Vernan diplomat's summary of foreign policy

**Verna** is a small independent republic beside [Vesper](factions.html#vesper-republic). It is known abroad less for armies or territory than for **scholarship**, **diplomacy**, **medicine**, **publishing**, **precision instruments**, **archives** and **scientific research**, and above all for the **University of Verna**, which is considerably more famous than the country that hosts it.

That fame is a mixed blessing. Vernans are used to foreigners talking as if the Republic exists merely to house the University. It does not. Verna was a republic before the great influx of scholars, and it remains a society of its own, with farmers, merchants, printers, civil servants and a great many people who have never set foot in a lecture hall.

This entry covers the Republic's history and its place among the powers. Its people and landscape are described in [[republic-of-verna|The Republic of Verna]], and the University itself in [[university-of-verna|The University of Verna]].

## Verna Before the Scholars

Before the refugees came, Verna was already an independent republic: small, politically stable, literate and commercially active. It had modest colleges of its own, respectable but not famous, where law, philosophy, medicine, rhetoric, mathematics and administration were most likely taught and preserved. When exactly the Republic was founded, and what those first colleges were called, are not recorded in the Archive's sources.

That history matters to Vernans, because it changes the story people tell about them. **The refugees did not bring learning to Verna. They found it there, and transformed it into something much larger.**

## The Scholars Arrive

The **Flight of the Scholars**, which followed the [[silencing-of-the-schools|Silencing of the Schools]] on the Old Scholastic Coast, brought professors, physicians, mathematicians, librarians, translators, instrument-makers, students and patrons to Verna. They came with copied archives, scientific tools and, most valuable of all, living teaching traditions.

Verna took them into its existing colleges. Over time, colleges merged, new faculties appeared, archives grew, and scholars from many intellectual traditions found themselves teaching side by side. The modern University grew out of that accumulation.

This is why Vernans are particular about one point. The University is not an Old Scholastic institution that happened to move house. It is **a Vernan institution, transformed by exile**.

> **Remembered in the history of one of the old colleges**
>
> The college's professor of mathematics had agreed, out of courtesy, to hear the newcomers lecture. He took a seat at the back, intending to stay for a quarter of an hour.
>
> He stayed for the whole afternoon. Then he came back the next day, and the next.
>
> At the end of the week he went to the rector's office. "There are three people in that room," he said, "each of whom knows more geometry than our entire faculty. I have checked. One of them is nineteen."
>
> "What do you propose?"
>
> "That we stop calling them guests."

## A Republic of Committees

Verna values **independence**, **neutrality**, **legal clarity**, **civic restraint**, **institutional continuity** and **scholarly autonomy**. Its politics are far less theatrical than Vesper's. Vernans are comfortable with committees, deliberation, legal agreements and procedure, and slightly suspicious of anyone who isn't.

Vernans like to put the difference from their neighbour this way: *Vesper argues in the street. Verna argues in committee, and publishes the minutes.* It is an exaggeration, but not much of one. How the Vernan government is organised in detail is not set down here.

## Neutrality by Treaty

Verna has little or no conventional offensive military power compared with the great powers. Its security rests instead on a network of **treaties**, **guarantees**, **alliances** and **diplomatic understandings**. The broad arrangement is:

- Verna stays politically neutral in major conflicts;
- Verna does not keep a large offensive standing army;
- foreign powers do not station permanent troops in Verna without broad agreement;
- neighbouring powers guarantee Verna's territorial integrity;
- and everyone treats Vernan independence as mutually useful.

The result is a deliberate paradox: **Verna preserves its independence by binding itself into agreements with stronger neighbours.** Vernans know this perfectly well. They simply prefer depending on treaties to depending on soldiers.

Other powers accept the arrangement because Verna is useful to nearly all of them. It is neutral ground, a centre of academic exchange and medical expertise, a publisher, a maker of fine instruments, an arbitrator, a host of international conferences and a keeper of archives. No great power particularly wants a rival to control it, which makes protecting it together convenient for everyone. Verna survives not by isolation but by **being valuable to everyone and owned by no one**.

Verna does keep internal security and civic protection, and probably some limited defensive forces. Exact treaty clauses, signatories and military limits are not recorded here.

> **At a dinner during an international conference in Verna**
>
> The foreign colonel had been looking around the hall with professional curiosity all evening.
>
> "Forgive me," he said to the Vernan beside him, "but I've seen your guards, and very smart they are. Where is your army?"
>
> The Vernan, a mild man from the Foreign Office, considered the question.
>
> "Yours is currently guaranteeing that we need not build one," he said, and passed the colonel the salt.

## Verna and the Other Powers

- **The [Vesper Republic](factions.html#vesper-republic).** Verna's closest major neighbour. They share intellectual exchange, academic culture, scientific enthusiasm and relatively secular public institutions, and differ sharply in style: Vesper favours openness, public argument and the fast circulation of knowledge; Verna favours preservation, evidence, controlled publication and institutional responsibility. They argue constantly about restricted research.
- **The [Aurelian Empire](factions.html#aurelian-empire).** Aurelia respects Vernan education, technical expertise, medical training and archival discipline, and is a valuable source of funding, infrastructure and institutional partnerships. Verna remains careful not to let state funding, imperial patronage or strategic interest steer its academic priorities. The relationship is cooperative but guarded.
- **The [Vardic Holds](factions.html#vardic-holds).** The Vards value Vernan theory, medicine, research and formal analysis, and Verna respects Vardic practical engineering. The tension is one of method: *Verna wants to study it first; the Vards want to test it.* Both sides benefit from the other more often than they admit.
- **The [Tianzhao Mandate](factions.html#tianzhao-mandate).** Strong mutual scholarly respect, built on a shared love of archives, long memory, classification, careful observation and continuity. Verna is fascinated by Tianzhao's vast records on ancestors, spirits, medicine, ritual and anomalous phenomena. Tianzhao does not grant unrestricted access to them. The relationship is intellectually rich and diplomatically polite.
- **The [Kharad Compact](factions.html#kharad-compact).** The most distant of Verna's major relationships. Trade and scholarly exchange continue, and Kharadi students attend the University, but Verna deliberately avoids becoming dependent on Kharadi credit, banking or merchant-house patronage, out of both historical memory and principle. The irony is not lost on anyone: Verna avoids one kind of dependency by relying on treaty guarantees from several other powers. Vernans prefer it that way. See [[silencing-of-the-schools|The Silencing of the Schools]].

> **In the corridor after a joint seminar, Vesperian and Vernan researchers**
>
> "Knowledge belongs to everyone," said the Vesperian, not for the first time that day.
>
> "So does the explosion," said the Vernan.

## Verna in Endros

Verna's reach in Endros comes almost entirely through the University: its laboratories, its researchers, the Expeditioners it sponsors and its close work with the Gate Evaluation Committee. On paper, the University governs Endros; in practice its authority covers the Ruins and little else. See [[university-of-verna|The University of Verna]] and Who Runs Endros?.
